37_marg4124: Scales. Jerome. Whence: “Thou shalt not have divers weights in thy bag, a greater and a less.” The balance shall be true and just for you, which is to be observed not only in trade but in all things. Whence: “Make a balance for thy words.”
37_marg4125: In Hebrew, efa; in Greek, ephi (corrupted). It pertains to the measure of dry produce: of wheat, barley, pulse.
37_marg4126: In Hebrew, bath: the same measure as the ephi, but only for liquids: wine, oil and the like.
37_marg4127: The core, which holds thirty modii, and in either measure, that is, of dry as well as liquid things, holds the first place: the tenth part of a core, in those things measured by the modius, is called an epha, that is, three modii; and the tenth part of a core in liquid kinds is called a bath.
37_marg4128: In which is signified the smallest little portion; whence: the whole world of riches belongs to him who is faithful. But he who is unfaithful possesses not even an obol, that is, nothing in the world, and lacks even the smallest portion. Of which: “He shall not go out thence till he pay the last farthing,” that is, the last and smallest number.
37_marg4129: R. We read of ten minas given for trading. And elsewhere: talents divided among servants. And debtors of ten denarii and of fifty. And the labourers of the vineyard, who each receive a denarius. And the woman who lost a drachma and, with the lamp lit, scarcely found it.
37_marg4130: The mina, which in Greek is mna, which has sixty sicles, that is, twelve hundred obols.
37_marg4131: The difficulty is set down in numbers so that it may make the hearer’s soul attentive, as also here: “He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.” For all prophecy has both truth and obscurity, so that the disciples may hear inwardly, and the ignoble crowd, set outside, may not know what is said.
37_interl15979: which we offer, while we attribute to God, who gives the fruits of virtue, whatever good we have, and not to ourselves
37_interl15980: while we teach men, that is, the rational animal, the mysteries of Scripture
37_marg4132: And these are the firstfruits, etc. Rabanus. According to the letter, the people were bound by the law to give the decades, that is, the tenth part of all fruits, to the Levites. Again, out of those tithes the Levites, that is, the lower ministers, gave tithes to the priests. There were also other tithes, which each one of the people of Israel set apart in his barns, that he might eat them when he went up to the temple in the city of Jerusalem, and in the porch of the temple, and invite the priests and Levites to banquets. And there were still other tithes, which they laid up for the poor. But the firstfruits which they offered from the crops were not fixed by a spiritual number but left to the choice of the offerers; and we have received a tradition of the Hebrews, not commanded by the law but put in place by the choice of the masters, that he who gave the most gave the fortieth part to the priests, he who gave the least, the sixtieth. And it was lawful to offer anything between the fortieth and the sixtieth, as they wished. What therefore was left in doubt in the Pentateuch is here defined spiritually, on account of the avarice of the priests, lest they demand more from the people, that is, that they offer the sixtieth part of what is produced from the earth. For if the cor, which in Hebrew is called omer, and by the Septuagint gomer, has thirty measures, in dry things as well as in liquids; and the ephi and the bath are the tenth part of the cor; and it is commanded that the sixth part of the ephi, as of the bath, be given to the priests in the firstfruits to be offered, which from three measures makes half a measure, it is plainly reckoned that the priests ought to receive the sixtieth part of the firstfruits.
37_marg4133: Of the core of barley. We give the firstfruits of barley when, being simple, we teach history. Whence: “Men and beasts thou wilt preserve, O Lord”; and then we say: “The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.” When we feed rational beings with wheat, we say with confidence: “Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me.” Let him who offers the firstfruits of wine and oil say: “Thou hast anointed my head with oil; and my chalice which inebriateth me, how goodly is it!” And when he has become an olive, let him say with the prophet: “But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God.” And the wine is from the true vine, who says: “I am the true vine, and you the branches; my Father is the husbandman.” This overflows in the winepresses of Christ, whence the psalms are entitled that refer to the sacraments of the Church.
37_marg4134: In the Old Testament the firstfruits were without measure or number, for “God doth not give the Spirit by measure.” But in the second building of the temple of Ezechiel there is a fixed measure, namely the sixtieth number, by which the world is completed. And it is said to us: “With what measure you mete, it shall be measured to you again.”
37_interl15982: Rabanus. That is, the oil which is prepared most pure for the lamps of the Lord.
37_interl15983: Whence: Christ, anointed above his fellows.
37_interl15985: of fine flour, meal and oil
37_interl15986: which is all burnt by holy fire
37_interl15987: when we are reconciled to God. Whence: “For Christ we beseech you, be reconciled to God.” And: “For God indeed was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself.”
37_marg4135: Above he said what part of those things that are weighed and measured, both of dry and of liquid kinds, ought to be offered to the prince; now he keeps the same order of firstfruits among living things, so that he commands one ram from a flock of two hundred to be offered.
37_marg4136: One ram out of the flock. It is shown that by the precept of the law the people are subject, so that they offer to the leader or prince, that through him the holocausts and sacrifices and libations may be offered by the people on each solemnity, and the house of God be expiated. For the prince in turn is a debtor to the people, that he may offer victims for them. Here, allegorically, it is Christ; here he takes up an animal, or a ram, which was nourished in well-watered places, that is, the Scriptures, according to Symmachus. And he can say: “The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing. In a place of pasture,” etc. “He hath brought me up on the water of refreshment.” These were the watered places, or rather the channels to which Jacob led his flocks, that they might drink there and conceive, and according to the color of the rods bring forth young for the Lord.
37_marg4137: This is the king, as is shown on the title of the cross in Hebrew, Greek and Latin letters. When the Jews tried to take away this triumphal title, they heard: “What I have written, I have written.”
37_interl15988: which is the church of the living God, which needs the expiation of sins
37_marg4138: The priestly dignity is admonished to what office it is bound, that it may know that it ought to offer, for the people, the sacrifice and the libations which are offered of wine, on all the solemnities, on the kalends, that is, the new moons, when, with darkness covering all things, the beginning of the moon’s light comes; and on the sabbaths, that is, the rest.
37_marg4139: On the sabbaths and on all the solemnities, etc. “My soul hateth your solemnities.” He who hates the solemnities of the Jews loves his own sabbath, namely that which is left to the people of God, that we may see the things that have been given us by God. For in the present age, which is “seated in wickedness,” we cannot see good days, but in the new one; whence: “Remember the days of old.” And elsewhere: “I had in my mind the eternal years.” Whence Isaias: “There shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath.”
37_interl15993: “Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth”; a young calf putting forth horns and hooves, in whom the sanctuary is cleansed
37_marg4140: In the first month, etc. Rabanus. Whence Isaias: “There shall be month after month, and sabbath after sabbath. And all flesh shall come to adore the Lord,” namely when the true adorers shall adore neither on mount Garizim nor in Jerusalem but in spirit and in truth; when there shall be a new heaven and a new earth, and “every creature shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God,” and the sun shall receive sevenfold light and the moon shall be likened to the sun. So the solemnities are spiritual, and the victims are spiritual.
37_interl15994: in whom the world is redeemed
37_interl15995: of the calf, which in other words is called the lamb: “Behold the Lamb of God, behold him who taketh away the sin of the world”; by whose flesh we are fed and by whose blood we are given to drink
37_interl15996: or of the temple, according to others, so that the house and altar are signified; for all the elements of the world are sanctified by this blood, so that when someone has been expiated and cleansed he may enter the gate of the inner court
37_marg4141: Rabanus. That, being cleansed, he may be able to know the secrets of the Lord, and consequently come to the seventh day of the first month and obtain rest, and offer sacrifice to the Lord, both for ignorance, of which it is said: “The sins of my youth and my ignorances do not remember,” and for the little child, who, when he shall have come to the measure of a perfect man, will say with confidence: “When I was a child, I spoke as a child,” etc. Or for him who has been deceived by error and has sinned not so much by will as by good opinion.
37_interl15997: of the same, namely of the month
37_interl15998: These two solemnities, namely the first day of the first month and the seventh of the same, are not held in the Mosaic law.
37_marg4142: In the first month, etc. When the two solemnities of the first month are completed, that is, of the first day and of the seventh of the same, he comes to the fourteenth day of the month, on which is the solemnity of the pasch; whence: “For Christ our pasch is sacrificed.” Then we shall eat unleavened bread for seven days, in the rest and security of all those things, when, destroying the leaven of malice and wickedness, we eat the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth; our Prince offering all things for us, and first for himself. He took up a human body, and “condemned sin in the flesh”; he grieved for us and bore our infirmities; then for his own house, which is written in the Septuagint but is not had in the Hebrew, that is, for the Church.
37_marg4143: Moses commanded this when we eat unleavened bread for seven days. But the fourth solemnity, of which he says: “In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month,” etc., seems to signify the feast of Tabernacles, which he has set down here without naming it.
37_interl16000: the human race; for the Saviour is the saviour of all men, and most of all of the faithful, and he himself is the propitiation for our sins, and not only for us but for the whole world
37_marg4144: When the calf has been offered for the whole people of the land, on the remaining seven days of the Lord’s passion seven calves and seven rams without blemish are offered daily, that they may be consumed in the holocaust and the fire of the Lord.
37_marg4145: Rabanus. The seven calves and seven rams are those who are configured to the Lord’s passion, that they may imitate the true calf and the true ram, and that through the seven days the sins of the whole world may be cleansed by the blood of the martyrs.
37_marg4146: Rabanus. It is to be carefully noted that in the sacrifice of the ephi, an ephi for a calf and an ephi for a ram, and a hin of oil are offered, as were commanded by the law. But in the offering of the he-goat neither an ephi nor, as the Septuagint translated, a boiling is set down; for they interpreted ephi itself as a boiling. The hin, however (which is a fixed measure of oil), is taken in the sacrifice of the calf and the ram, that we may deserve to receive the nourishment of the everlasting light, rest from labour, and healing of weariness, after the appeasing of sins.
37_marg4147: Rabanus. Also in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, in the solemnity of tabernacles, the same order of offering and of sacrifices is to be kept, as well for sin as for the holocaust, and in the sacrifice and in the oil, that, with darkness put to flight and the light of the oil risen, we may attain the feast of the Lord, and have brighter solemnities in which all our sins are forgiven us.
37_interl16002: whence: the sun of righteousness rises
37_interl16003: whence: Six days shalt thou labour, and shalt do all thy works
37_interl16004: that is, the seventh, in which is rest

37_marg4150: That is, when thirty days are completed, on the day of the new moon, which is the end of the higher month and the beginning of another; so that what privilege the seventh day has in the week, the month’s beginning may have this.

37_marg4152: That is, through the labours of this world and the gate of the Church, which is still set in earthly bounds; but he shall not enter the inner court, and he shall stand at the threshold of the inner gate.
37_marg4153: He shall stand at the threshold, etc. Rabanus. If the prince in the present writing does not enter the inner court but stands at its threshold, it is plain that now he can see in part and know in part, and cannot yet contemplate the glory of the Lord with face unveiled.
37_marg4154: For we need the mercy of God, and every creature, in comparison with the Creator, is unclean and must be purged by the divine fire. Whence in Isaias the lips were purged.

But after he who is first has gone out, the gate of the inner court itself will not be shut until the evening of this world, but will be open, that the people of the land also may be at the door and adore, not at every time, but when it has rested from sins and, with the darkness put to flight, has received the light of faith and knowledge.
37_interl16015: because above he had not given the number of the holocausts, here he gives it
37_marg4157: Rabanus. The holocaust, however, which the prince offers through the priests on the sabbath day, will be of six lambs without blemish, namely for the six days in which we work in the world. And a ram without blemish, who is the prince of the flock, so that with each ram an ephi, that is, the tenth part of a core, is offered in the sacrifice. But in the sacrifice of the six lambs no fixed measure is set, but as much as the hand of him who offers shall give, that is, according to the quality and measure of the works.
37_interl16018: that is, in the sacrifice of the ram

37_marg4158: Rabanus. He shall offer a hin of oil for each ephi (that is, the oil which the five virgins prepared for themselves), that he may anoint or mix the fine flour, and that every offering of God may be full of the light of truth, and the face of the offerer be made glad in oil.
37_marg4159: In the day, etc. The day of the new moons, namely, has this privilege beyond the sabbath day, that a calf of the herd is sacrificed, or, as others have translated, a bull without blemish; but the rest, that is, the six lambs without blemish and the ram without blemish, and their sacrifices, will keep the rite of the sabbath; so, namely, that as in the ram an ephi is offered for the sacrifice, that is, likewise, and a hin of oil, so it is offered also with the calf.
37_marg4160: And in the day of the calends. The thirtieth, namely, when the firstborn and the Levites are numbered in the law, a calf of the herd without blemish is offered for all Israel (on which we have treated more fully in the preceding chapter), and six lambs and rams without blemish, and the rest that are offered on the sabbaths, that we may attain eternal rest and deserve to hear: “Well done, good and faithful servant,” etc. And that we may be able not only to come to the gate of the inner court but also to enter, that being planted in the house of the Lord, “in the courts of the house of our God,” we may flourish.
37_marg4161: For he is of free will and has power to lay down his life and to take it up again; both coming to us and ascending to the heavens, he uses the same freedom of his majesty. Finally, he seeks no fairs or solemnities, nor observes any difference of days, because every time is a feast to him.
37_interl16024: the people enter and go out only at fairs and solemnities, and not by the same way but by one and another
37_marg4162: Rabanus. The people is commanded that if it has entered by the north gate to adore, it go out by the way of the south gate. This is the people of the Gentiles, which, leaving the north gate, from which evils break forth upon the earth, if it has entered the temple, ought not to go out except by the way of the south gate, that is, of light and heat, in which the bridegroom lies down at noon. Whence: “Arise, O north wind, and come, O south wind.” But he that goeth in by the way of the south gate, etc.: this is the people of the Jews, which, leaving the way of the gate of light, passes over to the north gate. Of which it is said: the north wind is a most hard wind; and: the pot of Jeremias is kindled from the face of the north. Otherwise: he enters by the north gate who gives up sins; he goes out by the south gate who follows virtues. Conversely, if the just man has fallen into sins, he enters indeed by the south gate, but goes out by the way of the north gate.
37_marg4163: For not only those who go out of Sodom are commanded not to look back, nor those who put their hand to the plough, that they look not behind them, but also those established in the house of the Lord, that they may not, namely, return to “the weak and needy elements,” and having begun in the spirit not be consummated in the flesh, but from spiritual things go on to greater (whence: “forgetting the things that are behind, I stretch forth myself to those that are before,” or the first), that they may not, namely, know in part but come to the perfect, as far as human frailty can, so that, namely, when they have done all things, they say: we are unprofitable servants. Whence Paul, as one imperfect: “Not that I have already attained.” And elsewhere, as one perfect, he says: “as many as are perfect,” etc. Hence it is plain that every man and the whole creature, though he has come to perfection, needs the mercy of God, and possesses full perfection by grace, not by merit.
37_interl16025: standing by as witness of both, namely of virtue or of sin
37_interl16026: of those entering, that is, and leaving. Whence: “there hath stood one in the midst of you, whom you know not.” And the Apostle: “Know you not that Christ is in you?”
37_marg4164: Rabanus. Whence the Apostle: “Know you not that Christ is in you?” If he is in those who do not know, how much more in those who know. But when the body shall have stood among those of knowledge, it will be dead because of sin, and the spirit shall live because of justice.
37_interl16028: of the sabbaths, that is, and of the new moons
37_marg4165: An ephi for a calf, etc. An ephi for each of the two is offered in the sacrifice. But with the lambs there is no fixed number, nor is the choice left to the will, but each uses the strength of a good conscience, that he may offer as much as he can, not as much as he wishes; and above all a hin of oil to every ephi, that the fine flour may be anointed and the lamp lighted in the sight of the Lord, and that those who use it may say: “But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God.”
37_interl16030: because it is voluntary, not another on his behalf
37_interl16031: Septuagint: salvations, because the reconciliation of peace offerings is the salvation of the one offering

37_marg4167: Which was not said above. For it is written: and the priests shall offer his holocaust and his peace offerings; and of the spontaneous and voluntary offerings nothing is said at all. When the prince has done this, the gate that looketh to the east will be opened to him. Of which: “This is the gate of the Lord, the just shall enter into it.” And whence the sun of justice rises.

37_marg4168: Rabanus. Not the priests for him, as is wont to be done on the sabbath day. But at every time the holocaust and peace offering which is offered voluntarily has the gate of the Lord open, nor does it keep the sabbath, but all days are reckoned as the sabbath, that is, rest.
37_marg4169: And a lamb of the same year, etc. Rabanus. 37_marg4170: Of the same year. Others: a yearling, because he preached the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution.
37_marg4171: He shall offer always in the morning, etc. Not at any hour, but when the sun has risen and it is the beginning of light, of which David: “In the morning thou shalt hear my voice.” “In the morning I will stand before thee, and will see.” And elsewhere: “At evening weeping shall have place, and in the morning gladness.” And: “O God, my God, to thee do I watch at break of day.”
37_marg4172: Let not the reader wonder if the same one is both prince and priest, and calf and ram and lamb, since in the Scriptures, according to the variety of reasons, we read that the same one is Lord and God and man and prophet and rod and root and flower and prince and judge and just king and justice, apostle and bishop, arm, servant, only-begotten, son, shepherd and firstborn, door, way, angel, arrow, and wisdom, and many things of the same kind.

37_interl16050: that is, if the prince could either take or seize, or under the appearance of honour hold, what is not his own, and leave it to his children
37_marg4175: He rebukes not only the priests or princes of that time but ours also, who become richer through the occasion of their dignity than they were before, that they take not from the poor by violence, nor under the name of honour despoil the rich, and leave nothing to their sons, to whom the paternal inheritance is due, except what was left to themselves by their parents. Therefore the priest who is richer, when he comes to the sacrifice, whatever more he has he ought to give not to his sons but to the poor and to the holy brethren, the household of the faith, who surpass the merits of books; and let him render to the Lord the things that are the Lord’s, who says: “As long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.” For he himself in his poor is received in hospitality, visited in prison, clothed when naked, given drink when thirsty, filled when hungry.
37_marg4176: Be dispersed, etc. Into parts is he dispersed who had been gathered in the name of the Lord; or, according to the law, the inheritance of one passes to another, and the line of division perishes, by which the inheritance came by lot to each one. But he disperses the people of God and takes away the everlasting possession of the faith, who leaves to sons, brothers and kinsmen goods that are another’s, whether by plunder or by flattery or by blandishments or under the pretext of religion.

37_interl16054: others: the chambers of the priests
37_marg4177: Toward the west. Others: the sea. For holy Scripture, describing the situation of Judea, often calls the sea the west. It is to be noted that the place of the priests, who boil the sacrifices for trespass or for ignorance and sin, that they may not be offered raw into the outer court, is placed to the west and the north, whence the coldest wind rises, where the light of the sun sets. From this it is shown that whatever pertains to food is either for error or for sin. But if a sacrifice is offered for ignorance, how much more for a trespass of conscience; whence in Job: “Lest perhaps my sons have sinned,” namely through ignorance.
37_marg4178: Rabanus. Who, namely, had not been prepared for sanctification, lest we readily give holy things to the unsanctified, or cast pearls before swine, or give what is holy to dogs. Whence Moses wishes the people to be sanctified for three days from all uncleanness and from the embrace of wives, that they may come to Mount Sinai and, sanctified, receive holy things. But if those who are to approach to hear the words of God and receive them are commanded to be sanctified from their wives, it is manifest that even in the law that apostolic saying is contained: “Defraud not one another, except, perhaps, by consent, that you may give yourselves to prayer.” And: by consent we must abstain from our wives that we may give ourselves to prayer.
37_interl16057: from the place of the priests, which faced north
37_interl16058: at each corner, namely, it had four little courts
37_marg4179: That from which he had gone out is clearly the inner one, and there are many courts in the holy Scriptures; whence: “You that stand in the house of the Lord, in the courts of the house of our God.” And Jesus says: “Other sheep I have, that are not of this court: them also I must bring, and there shall be one court and one shepherd.” For so it is in the Greek, which the Latin translator, unable to render fully in one word, rendered as “fold.” For when he says “of this court” he shows there is another, which is pointed out either in the crowd of the Gentiles, as distinct from Israel, or in the heavens, as distinct from the earthly court; for according to the quality of merits a court is assigned to each office.

37_marg4183: But the waters, etc. Rabanus. There are also bitter and very evil waters. Whence: “What hast thou to do with the way of Egypt, to drink the troubled water,” of Gihon, which in Hebrew is called Sior, that is, turbid and muddy. Whence: “I will give them the water of gall to drink,” that is, that in which dwells the dragon who said: “The rivers are mine,” etc. Whence: “The waters are come in even unto my soul.” And elsewhere: “Perhaps the water had swallowed us up.” This water is called by another name Mara, that is, bitterness, into which the wood of the cross is cast, and bitter things are turned into sweet. For the law of Moses, if it is understood in the sense of the flesh, is bitter, digging out “eye for eye, tooth for tooth”; see in Thamar fornication, and Osee joined to a harlot, Jeremias’s girdle, Moses’s Ethiopian wife, the killing of the Egyptian, and such things, which are bitter according to the killing letter and do not so much edify the reader as destroy him.
37_marg4184: But the waters came down. 37_marg4185: Not to the north, not to the west. Note that these waters, which flow out through the east gate, flee so far toward the left parts that they go to the south at the right side of the altar.
37_marg4186: It signifies that we cannot come at once to the east gate unless we come to it by the way of the north gate, by a long circuit. 37_marg4187: Rabanus. That we say cubitos in the masculine and not cubita in the neuter is not from ignorance of grammar but on account of the simple and unlearned, of whom the greater part is in the gathering of the church, we do.

37_marg4189: Rabanus. 37_marg4190: By these steps we come to the heights; yet these heights themselves reach up to the loins and reins, that all lust in us may be cut off, and we may possess the sanctification of the body, “without which no man shall see God.” Whence: from the feet up to the loins God is seen as fire. For the work of the loins needs fire and purging. Whence: “my loins are filled with illusions.” For by these the enemy mocks us night and day with phantasms; but from the loins up to the head and crown he shone with the most precious metal, with the brightness of amber, so that there is nothing foul in him, nothing of baseness.
37_marg4191: Rabanus. For neither the prophet nor human nature can cross the torrent of thoughts after the loins. Or the incitements of vices; but that man clothed in linen, the leader of the prophet, can clearly cross, who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.
37_marg4192: Who can glory that he has a clean heart? For the world is set in the wicked one; from childhood the heart of man is set toward evil, so that not even a man of one day, from the beginning of his birth, is without sin. Whence: “For behold I was conceived in iniquities; and in sins did my mother conceive me.” Not, that is, in the iniquities of my mother or my own, but those of the human condition. Whence: “death reigned from Adam unto Moses.”
37_interl16080: The aforesaid man, the leader of Ezechiel, warns the prophet in each thing that he look more carefully and see the hidden mysteries.
37_marg4193: Rabanus. In the figure, namely, of the Saviour. For Ezechiel is interpreted as the strength of God or dominion, and he is called son of man as a reminder of human frailty, lest he forget his condition while great things are shown to him.
37_marg4194: Rabanus. So that he who could not cross the middle depth may at least recognize those things that are on the banks.
37_marg4195: Rabanus. This torrent, which is borne along like a torrent by the abundance of its waters and receives the rains, is called a river by the Septuagint because it has perpetual waters, not gathered from rains here and there but flowing from a living and perpetual fountain. Of which: “The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful.” And elsewhere: “The river of God is filled with water.” And: “The floods have lifted up, O Lord, the floods have lifted up their voice.”
37_interl16083: which abound in paradise with various fruits, or trees.
37_interl16085: of baptismal grace, or evangelical teaching.
37_interl16086: from the threshold of the temple of the Lord.
37_interl16087: eastern, that is, the dead (sea), in which nothing could live, and which is very bitter; the Greeks call it asphaltum, that is, a pool of bitumen.
37_marg4196: That they, watering the plains and deserts, make the barren fruitful, and express the sacrament of the spring of Jericho, which Eliseus healed with the gospel and apostolic salt, so that where before there was barrenness and death, there might be fruitfulness and life.
37_marg4197: Rabanus. In a wonderful manner the dead waters, in which nothing can live, which have not known him who says, “I am the life,” are healed by the evangelical waters, whose torrents are to heal very many fishes, and all things shall live to which they come, so that fishermen stand on the banks from Engaddi even to Engallim. Engaddi is “fountain” or “eye.” Engallim is at the beginning of the dead sea, where the Jordan enters. Engaddi, where the dead sea is healed: I think this is that of which Zacharias says: “In that day living waters shall go out from Jerusalem, and the half of them to the former sea.” And Daniel: “the four winds of heaven were rushing upon the great sea.” And David: “wonderful are the elevations of the sea.” And: “I am come into the depth of the sea, and a tempest hath overwhelmed me.” The king of Egypt is called a dragon, who lies in the sea and stirs up the rivers as with his horns. And this sea is great and wide with hands. Unless it receives into itself the water of the river or torrent of God, it deadens what it has in itself. This most salt sea, and of exceeding bitterness, Christ healed by his death. Whence: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me: he hath sent me to preach to the meek, to heal the contrite of heart,” etc. And in Jeremias: “Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed,” etc. The angels also who were set over the Jews, when they cried, “His blood be upon us,” etc., and the veil of the temple was rent and all the sacraments of the Hebrews were laid open, answered the Lord who commanded: “We have cured Babylon, and she is not healed; let us forsake her,” that is, the city of confusion and of vices.
37_interl16089: to whom it is said: “I will make you to become fishers of men.”

37_marg4198: Very many kinds, etc. Rabanus. These fishes Peter drew to the right side at the Lord’s command, a hundred and fifty-three, so that for their multitude the nets were broken. Now those who have written on the natures of living creatures say that there are a hundred and fifty-three kinds of fishes, all of which were taken by the apostles, while they draw out of the sea of this world to salvation the noble and the lowly, the poor and the rich, and every kind of men.
37_interl16095: For whoever is not in the ark of Noe will perish in the flood. Likewise those whom this river does not touch are not saved.

37_interl16096: Whence: “And his leaf shall not fall off: and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.”
37_interl16097: And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, which shall bring forth its fruit in due season.
37_interl16098: As if these things come about because “its waters, etc.” Let us not think it is of the banks, or of the trees, or of such great abundant harvests; but because “its waters, etc.” For it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that showeth mercy.
37_interl16099: It shows the sacraments of the divine books, of which one part belongs to the letter and the other to the spirit.
37_interl16100: which contain moral teaching and give health, so that they heal the wounds of sinners
37_marg4200: Jerome. The tree of life, that is, wisdom, holds the chief place among all these trees. Of which it is said: “She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her.”
37_marg4201: The Septuagint. Its fruit. In its renewal it will give firstfruits, so that all the fruits of believers may be firstfruits, and each month be assigned to each apostle.
37_marg4202: And its leaves, etc. Rabanus. The Septuagint. Its ascent to health, so that, after the food of the fruits, we may by the warnings of words climb to heavenly things.
37_marg4203: Jerome. With the tribe of Levi removed, which was given over to the service of the Lord, the tribe of Joseph was divided into two, Ephraim and Manasses; which said to Josue: “Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to possess, whereas I am of so great a multitude, etc.”
37_marg4204: And you shall possess it, etc. Equally. Equal spaces of land, that is, according to their multitude, and not by the choice of the one dividing, but by lot, which stands by the power of the Lord. Josue himself also, the divider of the land, did not set apart a portion for himself, lest he seem to have chosen the best land for himself, but received it from the princes of all the tribes.
37_marg4205: And this is the border of the land, etc. Rabanus. The northern side begins from the great sea and by the way of Ethalon, which is interpreted “in the cradle of sorrow,” that is, through penance, comes to Sadada, where there is a turning aside at the side. For we understand the indignation, that is, of the Lord, hanging over us at Emath; or, when the truth of Emath has been found, the wells of Berotha are opened to us, which the princes Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob dug, and by a long circuit we come to the mountains of Sabarim, which are set between Damascus, that is, the blood of sackcloth, and the border of Emath, that is, of truth. For as through sorrow we turn aside from evils that threaten and avoid them at the side, so after the blood and sackcloth of a bloody life, before we come to the borders of Emath, we go around and come to the mountains. Of which it is said: “mountains are round about it”; which place is called the court of Tycon, that is, the middle, near the borders of Auran, that is, wrath, that we may say: “I will bear the wrath of the Lord, because I have sinned against him.” And from the sea to the borders of Damascus. In which Paul also, from Jewish fury and the shedding of the Church’s blood, beheld the light through blindness. And having taken sackcloth, through the pursuit of the old way he preached the gospel, that he might come to the court of the eternal fountain, and, once set in the north, lay hold of the border of truth.

37_marg4206: Rabanus. Allegorically. After the borders of the north, by a long circuit through Ethalon and Sadada and Berotha, Sabarim also and Thicon and Auran and Damascus and the court of Enon, one comes as far as Emath. The eastern side comes from the midst of wrath, that is, Auran, and from the midst of Damascus, that is, the blood of penance, and from the midst of Galaad, that is, of revelation or of the heap of witness, so that after wrath and penance it may show hope of salvation, and from the midst of the land of Israel, which holds the vision of peace, it reaches to the sweetest streams of the Jordan, which, the sea being far separated, receives the light of the east, so that it is ended by the river Jordan (which is interpreted “stream of judgment”) and by the bound of the torrent.

37_interl16118: which is in the desert of the Red Sea

37_marg4208: Rabanus. After the northern and eastern side, when the sun of justice has risen upon us, we receive the southern side, when the whole light is poured upon us from above, and when we enter with Abraham into the banquet and are inebriated with the wine that “maketh glad the heart of man”, with Joseph and his brethren. Now this possession begins from Thamar, that is, from the palm and the victory over vices, reaching even to the waters of contradiction. For virtues are always contradicted. Whence also the Jews, disputing against Paul, assert that the evangelical preaching is contradicted in the whole world. And elsewhere: “for a sign which shall be contradicted.” But all contradiction is holiness, which is the interpretation of Cades. Whence: “The Lord shall shake the desert of Cades”, which, that is, at first did not have the holiness of the Lord, but was shaken and moved that it might receive the guest of the Lord, who says: “Upon whom shall my spirit rest, but upon him that is humble and quiet, and that trembleth at my words.” After the desert of Cades, as far as the great sea, on the south of the southern side, is the torrent mentioned above, which has its waters not from the earth but from heaven, gathered together by the variety of diverse virtues.
37_marg4209: Rabanus. Allegorically. The west is always in the sea, always in the deep, always in the waves, where every day shipwrecks arise, and the deaths of the wretched, and loss of riches and merchandise; and yet when we have broken through all these by patience, we shall come straight on to Emath, that is, the truth of the Lord, who, persecutions having been overcome, has promised us eternal rewards.

37_marg4210: The possession of the holy land having been described, the possession of the individual tribes is described from the eastern side to the western side, that is, the sea. And first they receive their borders from the north, for those going by the way of Ethalon: Emath, the court, or Aserenon, the border of Damascus toward the north, by Emath. The first tribe begins with Dan. The second, Aser. The third, Nephthali. The fourth, Manasses. The fifth, Ephraim. The sixth, Ruben. The seventh, Juda; this on the left side, and the sevenfold number is completed. Then the firstfruits of the priests and Levites, and the sanctuary of the Lord in the midst, and the holy of holies. The city itself also is described, on each side a square, having four thousand five hundred reeds. The suburbs also of the priests and Levites, and the possession of the prince. And again on the right side five tribes follow, likewise from the eastern side to the western side. The first of these is Benjamin; the second Simeon, having his own possession specially, and not, as before, mixed with Juda. The third, Issachar. The fourth, Zabulon. The fifth, Gad; and the gates of the city, three on each side, and the name of the city, which is contained on the golden plate on the forehead of the high priest.
37_marg4211: It is to be noted that the names of the forty-eight cities which in the book of Numbers are given to the Levitical tribe to dwell in, with their suburbs, are here passed over in silence; as also the cities of the fugitives, of which three are beyond the Jordan, namely Bosor and Ramoth and Gaulon, in the two tribes and the half tribe, and three on this side of the Jordan, namely Cedes and Sichem and Cariatharbe. For in the mystical description, and the dwelling of the saints, and their perfect conversation, there was no need to describe the helps of fugitives, which Israel needed while still placed on earth; and Israel, coming in haste to this city through many labours and dangers, says in each of the saints: “I am a stranger and a sojourner.” And: “I have dwelt with the inhabitants of Cedar; my soul hath been long a sojourner.”
37_marg4212: And by the border of Aser, etc. After the borders of the seven tribes, the firstfruits are described from east to west.
37_interl16132: whose number is uncertain; for in the description of the individual tribes the measure is not fixed, but the length is always greater than the breadth
37_interl16134: from the east even to the sea
37_interl16136: which is referred to the five senses. Whence: you will possess the divine sense
37_interl16137: that you may be able to comprehend with all the saints what is the breadth, and length, that is, and depth, etc.
37_marg4213: It signifies consummate and perfect virtue, which through the decalogue of the Old Testament comes to the evangelical sacrament. For if, starting from one, you add the following number up to four, you will complete ten; and the Old Testament is bound together in the New, and the New will be opened out in the Old.
37_marg4214: Reading these things over, I can only say: “O the depth of the riches of the wisdom and of the knowledge of God!”
37_marg4215: Beside the border of the Levites are described the four quarters of the firstfruits of the sanctuary, which belong not to the people, nor to the base common crowd, nor to the Levites of lower rank, but properly belong to the worship of the priests.
37_marg4216: Isidore. That leaving the colds of the north we may come to the west, where our vices may set and perish. From there let us pass to the east, and the sun of justice having risen upon us, let us come to the south, in which the light of justice is for us most bright and perfect. And both from the north to the sea and from the east to the south, twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth, so that everywhere the same measure of length and breadth may be kept.
37_interl16145: that is, the just. Of whom: “The Lord is just, and hath loved justice”; here he says: “For neither doth the Father judge any man, but hath given all judgment to the Son”; of whom: “Give to the king thy judgment, O God: and to the king’s son thy justice.”
37_marg4217: Of whom above; who, that is, do not offer victims, but, content with the privilege of the name and the humility of their error, always say in the heart: “I know my iniquity, and my sin is always before me.” For it suffices the Arians and such as they, if they are not driven out of the temple, if they keep some shadow and image of their former name.
37_interl16147: that the Levites may have the border of the priests, but not its navel, that is, its middle, nor be able to hold that very possession.
37_marg4218: But the Levites also, etc. Isidore. The possession of the Levites is described, which is indeed next to the borders of the priests, and has the same space in length and breadth, on account of the multitude of the Levites, which the fewness of the priests has; yet it uses its own boundaries and understands that it is separated from the priestly rank, to repress the pride of the ministers, who, ignorant of the humility of their station, swell up above the priests.
37_marg4219: That the eternal possession of the Levitical distribution may remain, and the merit of their dignity not be overcome by price, nor be transferred from one to another, because what is sanctified to the Lord is not theirs to whom it is given, but his in whose name it is held.
37_interl16151: Of which: “The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful”; and “A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid.”
37_marg4220: Lay, that is, where the people may dwell anywhere; not that they are unclean, or that he thinks anything in the dwelling of the holy land is defiled, but because it is permitted to all except the priests to dwell there. By which we understand that all things which we refer to the senses, that is, to the pleasures of the body, which we take in by sight and hearing, touch, smell and taste, are profane, and do not have the sanctity of the temple, nor belong to the priestly privilege, but to lay vileness.
37_interl16153: and these are its measures; of the city.
37_marg4221: Isidore. When we have departed from the north wind, the coldest, we pass to the south; and after the light of knowledge has risen in us, we dread the setting of fortitude, considering not the past but the future, and not having a sure possession of virtue, but daily saying in prayer: “Lead us not into temptation”, one, that is, which we cannot bear.
37_marg4222: Each side of the city has four thousand five hundred reeds, which make eleven thousand and seventy-five paces, or, according to others, eight hundred and five, so that every city alike, as is written at the end of this volume, may have in its circuit eighteen thousand reeds, which make forty-four thousand and three hundred and forty paces. And the forty-fourth psalm is inscribed: “Unto the end, for them that shall be changed,” and it pertains to the beloved, namely the lovable one of the Lord. Or, according to Aquila, “for the lilies”; Symmachus, “for the flowers” of the Church, which is the city of the Lord and contains the sacraments; of which: “The queen stood on thy right hand, in gilded clothing; surrounded with variety.” And: “All the glory of the king’s daughter is within,” that is, inwardly, that it may not be like sepulchres whitened outwardly, but that she may wash everything of the dish, within and without.
37_marg4223: And the suburbs shall be, etc. These spaces go round the walls of the city in a circuit, to divide between the city and the rest. From which it is shown that no one has leave to work these spaces of the city or to gather their fruits, but that they are free from the use and work of men, so that around the walls the other parts of the city may have the pleasantness of shrubs and herbs growing of their own accord, and of the other things the earth brings forth.
37_marg4224: Reeds, namely, which have six cubits and one palm, and each side makes six hundred and seventeen paces, or nearly so; and in common, a thousand reeds, having two thousand four hundred and sixty-eight paces.
37_interl16156: who with words build the walls and mend what is broken and ruinous.
37_marg4225: After the description of the holy city and its suburbs, he says the rest is to be assigned to the workers of the city, namely the remaining part of the firstfruits of the sanctuary.
37_interl16157: let no one think himself exempt from the works of the city; let all eagerly build up the city.
37_marg4226: Out of all the tribes, etc. This was also done in the tabernacle: according to the variety of their means, one gives gold, another silver, scarlet, fine linen, purple, etc. And though the gifts differ in the quality of their substance, the reward of the givers is one; indeed it is greater for those who offer greater things according to their means, though small, like the poor widow in the Gospel.
37_interl16158: all the firstfruits of the twenty-five thousand; of the sanctuary.
37_marg4227: We briefly touch on this: that all the firstfruits of the sanctuary and the possession of the city, reckoned together by the square, contain two hundred and forty-six thousand and a third part. For if twenty-five thousand reeds, which have six cubits and one palm each, make by number, that is, by Roman reckoning, sixty-one thousand six hundred and sixty-seven paces, there is no doubt that these reckoned fourfold make the higher number. From which we perceive that all things are to be understood spiritually, and that the possession of the Church is much wider than that of the Levites once was in Judea, who did not even receive parts of the holy land, but from each tribe received, from forty-eight cities, not a possession in full but a dwelling and lodging; so that those too who seem to be laymen and have not come to the priestly and levitical rank, yet if they work in the city of the Lord, may feed on the holy land, the land of the meek and of the living; whence: “I believe to see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living.”
37_marg4228: Of whom above: he who receives as much as one tribe. But here we say that whatever remains out of all the tribes, he alone receives, so that there is no tribe that does not offer gifts to the prince, not from elsewhere but from the firstfruits which serve the temple and the sanctuary and the parts assigned to the city; and this is: “over against the five and twenty,” etc., so that the firstfruits may be between the seven and the five tribes, and in the firstfruits of the city and its suburbs, and in the midst of the city the sanctuary of the temple. But also of the possession of the city, whatever is left will be assigned to the prince; and the farthest part of the seven tribes, neighbouring the firstfruits and the city and the temple, in the tribe of Juda, and the farthest part of the five tribes, by the same right as above, in the tribe of Benjamin, and that farthest part itself will belong to the prince.
37_interl16160: But of the possession of the Levites and of the possession of the city, in the middle of the portions: whatever remains is assigned to the prince.
37_marg4229: And it shall belong to the prince, etc. By the same right that farthest part itself will belong to the prince; from which the sacraments of Holy Scripture are to be wondered at and thought on rather than spoken of. For in the former division, beyond the Jordan, the land was divided by Moses to two tribes, Ruben and Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasses. But on this side of the Jordan, by Josue the son of Nun and Eleazar the son of Aaron. Juda possessed on the south, and Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses on the north. Afterwards, however, when spies had been sent from Silo, and a description of the land by each tribe had been brought to Josue and to Eleazar, Benjamin received a possession beside Juda on the south, and beside Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasses. The second, the tribe of Simeon, received an inheritance in the tribe of Juda, that what was said might be fulfilled: “From Levi and Simeon I will divide them in Jacob, and will scatter them in Israel.” The third, Zabulon, received Galilee, in which is mount Thabor. The fourth, Issachar, where Jezrahel is, as far as the Jordan. The fifth, Aser, as far as mount Carmel, which overhangs the great sea, and Tyre and Sidon. The sixth, Nephthali, in Galilee as far as the Jordan, where is Tiberias, which was formerly called Chenereth. The seventh, Dan, as far as Joppe, where are the cities Ajalon and Selebi and Emmaus, which is Nicopolis. Although, as is read, they afterwards took for themselves, the other tribes having crossed over, the city Lesem, of the tribe of Dan, which is Paneas. Since these things are so, and there is so great a difference between the former description of the tribes and that which is now in our hands, it must be considered here how in the past too the city and temple were placed between the tribe of Juda and Benjamin. And in the former description indeed Juda was on the south and Benjamin on the north. But here the reverse, so that Juda is on the north and Benjamin on the south. After which the second is Simeon, the third Issachar, the fourth Zabulon, the fifth Gad, five tribes namely; whence also for the remaining tribes from the east side, etc.
37_interl16164: it signifies not a place but the waters in which the people contradicted the Lord and Moses offended.
37_marg4230: Which is now Palmyra, built by Solomon; for palm in Hebrew is called thamar, and it is now called Palmyra, perhaps because there are palm groves there.
37_marg4231: Isidore. The whole inheritance of the holy land is bounded on the south side by the borders of Egypt and the torrent of Rhinocorura. And because Gad is interpreted “temptation,” in the possession we pass from the palm-grove to the waters of contradiction, as far as Cades, which is interpreted “holy,” that we may understand that even after the victory over the world we ought always to be anxious in fear, mindful of that verse: temptation is the life of man upon earth; and that we come to holiness with adversaries resisting, and so obtain the victory; and from near by let us contemplate the torrent full of rains.
37_marg4232: Cades, etc. The same word in Hebrew sounds both torrent and inheritance, but here rather torrent, which enters the great sea, Rinocorule. Cades, however, is Batine in the desert, which extends as far as the city Petra.

37_marg4233: Concerning the circuit of the city, which on each side in the square had four thousand five hundred reeds, the preceding discourse foretold, which make eighteen thousand reeds, as is also set down in the present chapter, that is, forty-four thousand paces and three hundred and forty paces. Now it is written that on each side, that is, eleven thousand paces and eighty-five paces, there were three gates.

37_marg4235: And the gates of the city, etc. Isidore. These twelve gates or exits, according to the quality of merits and virtues, I judge to be joined to the single tribes, under the names of the apostles and the patriarchs. Of these it is written more openly in the Apocalypse of John. And within the mysteries of the divine Scriptures it is attested, and it is necessary, that such a city hold eighteen thousand reeds in circumference, under which number, in two from the twentieth psalm, the natural law and the grace of the gospel are described, by which the Church, that is, the city of the Saviour, is built up.
37_marg4236: This is briefly to be noted: that the same tribes encamped around the tabernacle in such a way that to the east were Juda, Issachar and Zabulon, sons of Lia; to the south Ruben, Simeon and Gad, two sons of Lia and a third, the son of Zelpha, Lia’s handmaid; to the west Ephraim, Manasses and Benjamin, two of them sons of Rachel, because Joseph, in place of the tribe of Levi, which was assigned to the sacrifices, was divided into two tribes, Ephraim and Manasses; to the north Dan, Nephthali and Aser, of whom the first and third are sons of Bala, Rachel’s handmaid, and the second the son of Zelpha, Lia’s handmaid, ignoble and placed to the north, being born indeed of handmaids at variance with one another. But this is according to the Book of Numbers and the description of the tabernacle, which was spoken by the mouth of Moses at God’s command. But our city, which is the city of the great king, whose builder and maker is God, of which it is said: “the most High himself hath founded her,” has another description and measure of the tribes in the holy land, and another order of possession and sides of the single tribes. First, three gates are set against the northern side, etc., of whom the firstborn is Ruben, Juda the author of the royal stock, and Levi. Concerning whose name nothing is said in the description of the tabernacle and the camp, so that, possessing the birthright as a royal and priestly race, we may despise the cold of the north.
